function.name: run_bash
function.description:
Execute a non-interactive bash command in a working directory. Any provided cwd must be an absolute path to an existing accessible local directory, including one outside the workspace. If cwd is omitted, the workspace root is used when available, otherwise the system temporary directory. cwd applies only to this invocation and does not change workspace identity or persist across calls. The result includes effectiveCwd so you can confirm where the command actually ran.

For long-running work (builds, test suites, dev servers) set run_in_background: the call returns at once with the command's pid and outputFile, and when it ends you are told its exit code (or signal) and last output lines, without polling. Read its output with `tail -n 50 <outputFile>` and stop it with `kill <pid>`, which stops everything the command started.

An `&` job of a foreground command that is still running when the foreground part ends is a background task too: the call returns, the result lists it in backgroundTasksStarted, and you are told when it ends. `kill <pid>` on such a job stops that process only; use run_in_background when you need to stop a command together with the processes it starts. Tasks started by one call share its outputFile. A background task that ends while one of your run_bash calls runs is reported in that call's backgroundTasksEnded instead of a later notice. Processes that detach themselves (nohup, setsid, disown) are not tracked. Background commands are stopped and their output files removed when your run ends.

cwd.description: Optional working directory for the command.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time in seconds for the command's foreground part. Does not apply with run_in_background.

run_in_background.description: Run the command in the background: the call returns at once with its pid and outputFile, and you are notified when it ends.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Reads content from a specified file. Supports optional 1-based inclusive line ranges via start_line/end_line. Each returned line is prefixed with its line number when include_line_numbers is true. Image, audio and video files (by extension) are attached for the model to see in the next turn instead of being returned as text; line ranges do not apply to them, a kind the current model cannot take is refused, and other binary files are refused. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute base_dir and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell cd state. Raises ValueError if a relative path is given without an absolute base_dir or if line range arguments are invalid. Raises FileNotFoundError if the file does not exist. Raises IOError if file reading fails for other reasons.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path, or a relative file path paired with base_dir. If path is relative, you must provide an absolute base_dir. If base_dir is omitted, path must be absolute. Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. Do not provide a relative base_dir.

start_line.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Text files only; omit to start at line 1.

end_line.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Text files only; omit to read to the end.

include_line_numbers.description: If true, prefix each returned line with its line number (default).

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Applies a context-located patch to one file using a simplified unified-diff-style format, without overwriting unrelated content. Before calling `edit_file`, read the current relevant file region unless it was just read and has not changed. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from that latest content; do not reconstruct them from memory. After an intervening edit or a context-match failure, read the affected region again before retrying. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute `base_dir` and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell `cd` state. Use this for surgical edits; use `write_file` only for a deliberate whole-file rewrite.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path, or a relative file path paired with base_dir. If path is relative, you must provide an absolute base_dir. If base_dir is omitted, path must be absolute. Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. Do not provide a relative base_dir.

patch.description:

Every prefixed hunk body record is a complete logical line even if the outer patch string has no final line ending. Outer patch-string termination is transport framing, not target-file semantics. To make changed target content end without a line terminator, immediately follow that record with the exact marker `\ No newline at end of file`; this marker is the sole opt-out from a changed record's normal line terminator. Include enough unchanged or removal lines to identify exactly one eligible location.

Example patch:
@@
-const mode = 'old'
+const mode = 'new'
 const keep = true

function.name: list_project_tasks
function.description: List the Tasks in the explicit project_id, optionally filtered by exact TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE or CANCELLED status (CANCELLED = dropped as not needed). Each Task's taskId is its key (e.g. autobyteus-42): use it as the Task's ID in every tool. Each Task is a short entry: taskId, title, status, the Tasks it depends on (dependsOn, by taskId), the bigger Task it is part of (partOf, a taskId), its parts (parts, by taskId), its number of comments (commentCount) and its open assignments (assignments). A field with no value is left out (for example partOf when the Task is part of no bigger Task). Each assignment names the task agent: {kind: agent, agentRunId} for a task agent, or {kind: team, teamRunId, teamCoordinatorAgentRunId} for a task agent team; plus who assigned it (assignedBy) and whether the work was accepted (outcome); accepted work is not necessarily finished. Give a follow-up Task to a task agent with delegate_task and its target_agent_run_id (agentRunId) or target_team_run_id (teamRunId); talk with it using send_message_to and its run id (agentRunId, or teamCoordinatorAgentRunId for a task agent team). A Task whose assignments can't be read is marked assignmentsUnavailable. A Task's description, comments, context files and closed assignments are not listed; get_project_task, when you have it, reads one Task in full.

project_id.description: Explicit Project identity on the current node.

function.description: Search the Tasks of the explicit project_id with a sentence or a few words (query) describing the work: by meaning (related wording, paraphrases) and by exact text. project_id.description: Explicit Project identity on the current node.

query.description: A sentence or a few words describing the Task you are looking for.

function.name: search_memory
function.description: Search the memory of all agent runs on this node (their Work Journals: what each run did, with dates) by words and by meaning, in any language. Use it whenever the user or the task refers to earlier work: "do you remember", "last time", "earlier we", "before", "where is the … we set up", or a decision, setup or file made in a past conversation. Each result names who (agent, and team or org with member when there is one), runId, workspace, the first and latest day mentioned, a source line to cite, and its matches: journalFile (an absolute path), lines, day, a short snippet and matchedBy. query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words, any language: a sentence or a few words.

limit.description: Most runs returned, 1 to 20 (default from the server setting).

A task_id that names no Task of that Project fails with TASK_NOT_FOUND. If you work on a Task (it was delegated to you or to your task team, or you do part of a task agent's work), you can read only that Task; another Task fails with TASK_READ_OUT_OF_SCOPE. project_id.description: Explicit Project identity on the current node.

task_id.description: The Task's ID: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42, any letter case) or its long ID, in that Project.

function.name: create_task
function.description: Create a Project Task: supply project_id, a required title (the Task's one-line name, shown wherever the Task is listed) and a required description (the Task's content); omit status and task_id. Optional depends_on: the taskIds of Tasks of the same Project that come first (or that this Task follows up); it only informs and never stops work. Optional part_of: the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts). Returns the recorded Task (projectId, taskId, title, status, dependsOn, partOf) plus attachedContextFiles [{name, path}] when files were attached; a field with no value is left out. project_id.description: Project identity on the current node.

title.description: The Task's one-line name: trimmed, non-empty; no length limit.

description.description: Trimmed non-empty Task content.

context_files.description: Absolute local file paths on this node to copy into the new Task's saved context. Same file types and size limits as the app.

depends_on.description: taskIds (keys, e.g. autobyteus-39) of Tasks in the same Project that this Task depends on.

part_of.description: The taskId (key, e.g. autobyteus-25) of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts).

function.name: update_task
function.description:
Update a Task by its task_id: a Project Task (its key, e.g. autobyteus-42), or the Task a description-only delegate_task created (it has no Project; delegate_task returned its task_id). Supply title and/or description and/or status (TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, CANCELLED) and/or context_files and/or depends_on and/or part_of and/or add_comment; never project_id.
DONE means the work is finished; CANCELLED means the Task was dropped as not needed (not finished). Both end this Task's work for its task agents; a task agent is stopped when this was its last open Task; their history is kept. Close a Task you delegated when its work is done. Setting a Task that has parts to DONE or CANCELLED also sets its open parts the same way (ending their work for their task agents, as above); closedParts lists them.
To continue a closed Task with the same task agent, first set the Task to TODO or IN_PROGRESS; then, if you assigned the Task, message the task agent's run id (for a task agent team, its coordinator's run id): it continues with its conversation. A status change alone starts nothing. To give a task agent another Task, also while its other Tasks are open, use delegate_task with its target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.
Optional title (Project Tasks only): the Task's new one-line name.
Optional depends_on (Project Tasks only): the complete list of taskIds of Tasks of the same Project this Task depends on; it replaces the saved list, [] clears it. It only informs and never stops work.
Optional part_of (Project Tasks only): the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts); "" clears it.
Optional add_comment (Project Tasks only): text added as a new comment at the end of the Task's comments; the description is not changed. Each call adds one comment.
Optional context_files: absolute local file paths copied into a Project Task as context files; appended, never removed. Same file types and size limits as the app; not for a Task with no Project. Any invalid file fails the whole call with no change. Unknown IDs fail; omitted fields, saved context, dependencies and the parent are kept. Returns the recorded Task identity (taskId; projectId and title for a Project Task) and status, plus dependsOn and partOf for a Project Task, attachedContextFiles [{name, path}] when the call attached files, closedParts when it closed parts and partsNotClosed when it could not close some of them; a field with no value is left out (a Task with no Project has no projectId, title, dependsOn or partOf).

task_id.description: The Task's ID: a Project Task's key (e.g. autobyteus-42), or the Task ID of a Task with no Project.

title.description: Project Tasks only: the Task's new one-line name, trimmed non-empty; omit to preserve.

description.description: Trimmed non-empty Task content; omit to preserve.

status.description: Explicit business status patch; omit to preserve.

context_files.description: Absolute local file paths on this node to copy into the Project Task's saved context (appended; never removes). Same file types and size limits as the app.

depends_on.description: Project Tasks only: the complete list of taskIds of Tasks in the same Project this Task depends on; replaces the saved list, [] clears it, omit to keep.

part_of.description: Project Tasks only: the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts). Replaces the saved one; "" clears it; omit to keep.

add_comment.description: Project Tasks only: text added as one new comment at the end of the Task's comments; the description is not changed.

function.name: list_available_agents
function.description: List the agents and agent teams you can work with, each with its name, kind (agent or agent_team), address and description (when it has one). With node, list what that peer node offers for delegation instead; use an address from that list as recipient_address in delegate_task with the same node. This tool is read-only.

node.description: Optional: the name of a peer node registered on this node. Without it, this node's agents and agent teams are listed.

function.name: list_peer_nodes
function.description: List the peer nodes registered on this node, each with its name and status: available (it takes work from this node now) or unavailable. Use the name as node in list_available_agents and delegate_task; for an unavailable node, list_available_agents with that node says why. This read-only tool takes no arguments.

function.name: delegate_task
function.description:
Delegate a task to an agent or agent team. Use exactly one mode:
(1) recipient_address and description, with optional reference_files: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) that works on the task you describe;
(2) recipient_address and task_id: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) for that saved Task (its description and files);
(3) exactly one of target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id, with task_id: gives the saved Task to one of your task agents (or task agent teams), which continues with its conversation; use it for follow-up work that builds on what that task agent already did. This works only when you made its most recent assignment; its other open Tasks stay open, and it is freed when its last Task is closed.
With node in mode (1), the task agent starts on that peer node, from the agent or agent team at recipient_address there; the result also gives node, and you message it by its run id as usual. A saved Task or reference_files can't go to another node.
Never supply project_id. Delegating to yourself, a teammate or your own team is refused.
The task description and reference files become the task agent's first message (for a task agent team, its coordinator receives them), together with your run id.
If you are a task agent yourself (another agent delegated your task to you or to your team), task_id is refused, and a delegation with a description returns no task_id: the new task agent's work is part of your Task. Otherwise, a delegation with a description also creates a Task with no Project and returns its task_id.
On success, delegated is true, target_kind is agent or team, and the result names the task agent: target_agent_run_id for a task agent; for a task agent team, target_team_run_id (the team; use it to give the team a later Task) and target_team_coordinator_agent_run_id (its coordinator; talk with the team through this run id). launch_notes, when present, says which agent runs on a different runtime or model than configured. If delegated is false, nothing was created and message says why; correct the problem and delegate again, or report the failure.

recipient_address.description: Only for a new task agent: the exact address of an available agent or agent team, beginning with '/'. Every call with an address creates another task agent or task agent team. Omit it when you give a Task to one of your task agents with target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.

target_team_run_id.description: One of your task agent teams, by the target_team_run_id an earlier delegation returned (the team's run id, not its coordinator's). Supply only it and task_id.

target_agent_run_id.description: One of your task agents, by the target_agent_run_id an earlier delegation returned. Supply only it and task_id. A task agent team's coordinator's run id is refused: use target_team_run_id for a task agent team.

task_id.description: A saved Project Task's ID on this node: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42), as list_project_tasks shows it; its saved text and files are used. With recipient_address: a new task agent works on the Task. With target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id: that task agent takes on the Task. Blank, unknown, ambiguous, DONE or CANCELLED Tasks fail.

description.description: Only with recipient_address and without task_id. A complete, ready-to-work task description: objective, context, scope, constraints, what done looks like, expected output and reference guidance.

node.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description: the name of a peer node registered on this node. The new task agent then runs on that node, and recipient_address is the address of an agent or agent team on that node.

reference_files.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description; not allowed with task_id, not even as an empty list. Absolute local file paths the task agent should read. Relative paths and URLs are rejected.

function.name: send_message_to
function.description:
Send a self-contained request, result, question or blocker to an agent or agent team that already exists. Use exactly one selector, never both:
- recipient_address: an exact address beginning with '/'. A team's address reaches its coordinator. An address inside your own team reaches the member of your own team.
- target_agent_run_id: an agent's run id. For a task agent team, use its coordinator's run id; a team's own run id is refused.
send_message_to never creates an agent; to have work done by a new agent, use delegate_task. It returns the run id of the agent that received the message as target_agent_run_id, or leaves it out, with the reason, when the message can't be delivered.

recipient_address.description: An exact address beginning with '/'. Relative addresses, bare names and '/' alone are not valid.

target_agent_run_id.description: An agent's run id. Unknown run ids are rejected.

content.description: Self-contained work request, result, or specific blocker. State the requested work or outcome and relevant context; include important absolute paths here and put files the recipient should inspect in reference_files. Example: 'Implementation is ready. The handoff is at /Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md and the test log is at /Users/me/project/test.log; please review the risks below.'

reference_files.description: Optional attachment/reference list of absolute local file paths the recipient may need to inspect. Use this in addition to self-contained content, not instead of explaining the handoff. Example: ['/Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md', '/Users/me/project/test.log'].

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. function.name: list_project_tasks
function.description: List the Tasks in the explicit project_id, optionally filtered by exact TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE or CANCELLED status (CANCELLED = dropped as not needed). Each Task's taskId is its key (e.g. autobyteus-42): use it as the Task's ID in every tool. Each Task is a short entry: taskId, title, status, the Tasks it depends on (dependsOn, by taskId), the bigger Task it is part of (partOf, a taskId), its parts (parts, by taskId), its number of comments (commentCount) and its open assignments (assignments). A field with no value is left out (for example partOf when the Task is part of no bigger Task). Each assignment names the task agent: {kind: agent, agentRunId} for a task agent, or {kind: team, teamRunId, teamCoordinatorAgentRunId} for a task agent team; plus who assigned it (assignedBy) and whether the work was accepted (outcome); accepted work is not necessarily finished. Give a follow-up Task to a task agent with delegate_task and its target_agent_run_id (agentRunId) or target_team_run_id (teamRunId); talk with it using send_message_to and its run id (agentRunId, or teamCoordinatorAgentRunId for a task agent team). Returns the best-matching Tasks first, at most limit (default 10, 1 to 30), each with its taskId (its key, e.g. autobyteus-42), status, partOf and parts (as in list_project_tasks), title, commentCount and match (exact: the title, the description or a comment contains the query; meaning: related by meaning); a field with no value is left out. meaningSearch is present only when meaning search was not fully used: it says whether it is preparing or unavailable, and note says why and which results are exact text matches only. query.description: A sentence or a few words describing the Task you are looking for.

function.name: search_memory
function.description: Search the memory of all agent runs on this node (their Work Journals: what each run did, with dates) by words and by meaning, in any language. Use it whenever the user or the task refers to earlier work: "do you remember", "last time", "earlier we", "before", "where is the … we set up", or a decision, setup or file made in a past conversation. Returns up to limit runs (1 to 20; default from the server setting, normally 10), best first. Each result names who (agent, and team or org with member when there is one), runId, workspace, the first and latest day mentioned, a source line to cite, and its matches: journalFile (an absolute path), lines, day, a short snippet and matchedBy. A text match lists the query words it contains (matchedWords); a match without matchedWords was found by meaning. wordsNotFound names query words that occur in no indexed journal (the index follows new turns within about a minute). Results are pointers, not facts: open a run's first match (its newest) at its lines with your file tool before answering, and the second when the first does not answer, before searching again. Answer from the run you read and cite its source. When several runs differ, prefer the latest mention and say so. If what you read does not answer the question, try other words. coverage says how much is indexed while indexing is incomplete; with no index yet, ask the user to start it on the Memory page.

query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words, any language: a sentence or a few words.

limit.description: Most runs returned, 1 to 20 (default from the server setting).

function.name: update_task
function.description:
Update a Task by its task_id: a Project Task (its key, e.g. autobyteus-42), or the Task a description-only delegate_task created (it has no Project; delegate_task returned its task_id). Supply title and/or description and/or status (TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, CANCELLED) and/or context_files and/or depends_on and/or part_of and/or add_comment; never project_id.
DONE means the work is finished; CANCELLED means the Task was dropped as not needed (not finished). Both end this Task's work for its task agents; a task agent is stopped when this was its last open Task; their history is kept. Close a Task you delegated when its work is done. Setting a Task that has parts to DONE or CANCELLED also sets its open parts the same way (ending their work for their task agents, as above); closedParts lists them.
To continue a closed Task with the same task agent, first set the Task to TODO or IN_PROGRESS; then, if you assigned the Task, message the task agent's run id (for a task agent team, its coordinator's run id): it continues with its conversation. A status change alone starts nothing. To give a task agent another Task, also while its other Tasks are open, use delegate_task with its target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.
Optional title (Project Tasks only): the Task's new one-line name.
Optional depends_on (Project Tasks only): the complete list of taskIds of Tasks of the same Project this Task depends on; it replaces the saved list, [] clears it. It only informs and never stops work.
Optional part_of (Project Tasks only): the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts); "" clears it.
Optional add_comment (Project Tasks only): text added as a new comment at the end of the Task's comments; the description is not changed. Each call adds one comment.
Optional context_files: absolute local file paths copied into a Project Task as context files; appended, never removed. Same file types and size limits as the app; not for a Task with no Project. Any invalid file fails the whole call with no change. Unknown IDs fail; omitted fields, saved context, dependencies and the parent are kept. function.name: delegate_task
function.description:
Delegate a task to an agent or agent team. Use exactly one mode:
(1) recipient_address and description, with optional reference_files: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) that works on the task you describe;
(2) recipient_address and task_id: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) for that saved Task (its description and files);
(3) exactly one of target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id, with task_id: gives the saved Task to one of your task agents (or task agent teams), which continues with its conversation; use it for follow-up work that builds on what that task agent already did. This works only when you made its most recent assignment; its other open Tasks stay open, and it is freed when its last Task is closed.
With node in mode (1), the task agent starts on that peer node, from the agent or agent team at recipient_address there; the result also gives node, and you message it by its run id as usual. A saved Task or reference_files can't go to another node.
Never supply project_id. Delegating to yourself, a teammate or your own team is refused.
The task description and reference files become the task agent's first message (for a task agent team, its coordinator receives them), together with your run id.
If you are a task agent yourself (another agent delegated your task to you or to your team), task_id is refused, and a delegation with a description returns no task_id: the new task agent's work is part of your Task. Otherwise, a delegation with a description also creates a Task with no Project and returns its task_id.
On success, delegated is true, target_kind is agent or team, and the result names the task agent: target_agent_run_id for a task agent; for a task agent team, target_team_run_id (the team; use it to give the team a later Task) and target_team_coordinator_agent_run_id (its coordinator; talk with the team through this run id). launch_notes, when present, says which agent runs on a different runtime or model than configured. If delegated is false, nothing was created and message says why; correct the problem and delegate again, or report the failure.

recipient_address.description: Only for a new task agent: the exact address of an available agent or agent team, beginning with '/'. Every call with an address creates another task agent or task agent team. Omit it when you give a Task to one of your task agents with target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.

target_team_run_id.description: One of your task agent teams, by the target_team_run_id an earlier delegation returned (the team's run id, not its coordinator's). Supply only it and task_id.

target_agent_run_id.description: One of your task agents, by the target_agent_run_id an earlier delegation returned. Supply only it and task_id. A task agent team's coordinator's run id is refused: use target_team_run_id for a task agent team.

task_id.description: A saved Project Task's ID on this node: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42), as list_project_tasks shows it; its saved text and files are used. With recipient_address: a new task agent works on the Task. With target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id: that task agent takes on the Task. Blank, unknown, ambiguous, DONE or CANCELLED Tasks fail.

description.description: Only with recipient_address and without task_id. A complete, ready-to-work task description: objective, context, scope, constraints, what done looks like, expected output and reference guidance.

node.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description: the name of a peer node registered on this node. The new task agent then runs on that node, and recipient_address is the address of an agent or agent team on that node.

reference_files.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description; not allowed with task_id, not even as an empty list. Absolute local file paths the task agent should read. Relative paths and URLs are rejected.

function.name: send_message_to
function.description:
Send a self-contained request, result, question or blocker to an agent or agent team that already exists. Use exactly one selector, never both:
- recipient_address: an exact address beginning with '/'. A team's address reaches its coordinator. An address inside your own team reaches the member of your own team.
- target_agent_run_id: an agent's run id. For a task agent team, use its coordinator's run id; a team's own run id is refused.
send_message_to never creates an agent; to have work done by a new agent, use delegate_task. It returns the run id of the agent that received the message as target_agent_run_id, or leaves it out, with the reason, when the message can't be delivered.

recipient_address.description: An exact address beginning with '/'. Relative addresses, bare names and '/' alone are not valid.

target_agent_run_id.description: An agent's run id. Unknown run ids are rejected.

content.description: Self-contained work request, result, or specific blocker. State the requested work or outcome and relevant context; include important absolute paths here and put files the recipient should inspect in reference_files. Example: 'Implementation is ready. The handoff is at /Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md and the test log is at /Users/me/project/test.log; please review the risks below.'

reference_files.description: Optional attachment/reference list of absolute local file paths the recipient may need to inspect. Use this in addition to self-contained content, not instead of explaining the handoff. Example: ['/Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md', '/Users/me/project/test.log'].

ANTHROPIC.name: run_bash
ANTHROPIC.description:
Execute a non-interactive bash command in a working directory. Any provided cwd must be an absolute path to an existing accessible local directory, including one outside the workspace. If cwd is omitted, the workspace root is used when available, otherwise the system temporary directory. cwd applies only to this invocation and does not change workspace identity or persist across calls. The result includes effectiveCwd so you can confirm where the command actually ran.

For long-running work (builds, test suites, dev servers) set run_in_background: the call returns at once with the command's pid and outputFile, and when it ends you are told its exit code (or signal) and last output lines, without polling. Read its output with `tail -n 50 <outputFile>` and stop it with `kill <pid>`, which stops everything the command started.

An `&` job of a foreground command that is still running when the foreground part ends is a background task too: the call returns, the result lists it in backgroundTasksStarted, and you are told when it ends. `kill <pid>` on such a job stops that process only; use run_in_background when you need to stop a command together with the processes it starts. Tasks started by one call share its outputFile. A background task that ends while one of your run_bash calls runs is reported in that call's backgroundTasksEnded instead of a later notice. Processes that detach themselves (nohup, setsid, disown) are not tracked. Background commands are stopped and their output files removed when your run ends.

cwd.description: Optional working directory for the command.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time in seconds for the command's foreground part. Does not apply with run_in_background.

run_in_background.description: Run the command in the background: the call returns at once with its pid and outputFile, and you are notified when it ends.

Image, audio and video files (by extension) are attached for the model to see in the next turn instead of being returned as text; line ranges do not apply to them, a kind the current model cannot take is refused, and other binary files are refused. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute base_dir and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell cd state. Raises ValueError if a relative path is given without an absolute base_dir or if line range arguments are invalid. Raises FileNotFoundError if the file does not exist. Raises IOError if file reading fails for other reasons.

ANTHROPIC.description: Applies a context-located patch to one file using a simplified unified-diff-style format, without overwriting unrelated content. Before calling `edit_file`, read the current relevant file region unless it was just read and has not changed. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from that latest content; do not reconstruct them from memory. After an intervening edit or a context-match failure, read the affected region again before retrying. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute `base_dir` and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell `cd` state. Use this for surgical edits; use `write_file` only for a deliberate whole-file rewrite.

Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. patch.description:
Patch content in a simplified unified-diff-style format. Start every hunk with a bare `@@` line. Prefix unchanged lines with one space, removals with `-`, and additions with `+`. Every prefixed hunk body record is a complete logical line even if the outer patch string has no final line ending. Outer patch-string termination is transport framing, not target-file semantics. To make changed target content end without a line terminator, immediately follow that record with the exact marker `\ No newline at end of file`; this marker is the sole opt-out from a changed record's normal line terminator. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from the latest current file content. The target file is identified by the separate `path` argument; inside `patch`, provide only bare context hunks. Do not include Git file headers (`diff --git`, `---`, or `+++`), numeric hunk coordinates, or semantic envelopes such as `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch`. Include enough unchanged or removal lines to identify exactly one eligible location.

Example patch:
@@
-const mode = 'old'
+const mode = 'new'
 const keep = true

Use it whenever the user or the task refers to earlier work: "do you remember", "last time", "earlier we", "before", "where is the … we set up", or a decision, setup or file made in a past conversation. Returns up to limit runs (1 to 20; default from the server setting, normally 10), best first. Each result names who (agent, and team or org with member when there is one), runId, workspace, the first and latest day mentioned, a source line to cite, and its matches: journalFile (an absolute path), lines, day, a short snippet and matchedBy. A text match lists the query words it contains (matchedWords); a match without matchedWords was found by meaning. wordsNotFound names query words that occur in no indexed journal (the index follows new turns within about a minute). Results are pointers, not facts: open a run's first match (its newest) at its lines with your file tool before answering, and the second when the first does not answer, before searching again. Answer from the run you read and cite its source. When several runs differ, prefer the latest mention and say so. If what you read does not answer the question, try other words. coverage says how much is indexed while indexing is incomplete; with no index yet, ask the user to start it on the Memory page.

query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words, any language: a sentence or a few words.

limit.description: Most runs returned, 1 to 20 (default from the server setting).

ANTHROPIC.description: Read one Project Task in full: supply project_id and task_id (the Task's key, e.g. autobyteus-42, in any letter case, or its long ID). Returns projectId, taskId (its key), title, status, description, dependsOn and partOf and parts (by taskId), comments (their texts, oldest first), contextFiles ([{name, path}]: read a file by its path), assignments and closedAssignments (one per earlier assignment period; each as in list_project_tasks); a field with no value is left out. A task_id that names no Task of that Project fails with TASK_NOT_FOUND. If you work on a Task (it was delegated to you or to your task team, or you do part of a task agent's work), you can read only that Task; another Task fails with TASK_READ_OUT_OF_SCOPE. Read-only; Tasks with no Project are not read.

task_id.description: The Task's ID: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42, any letter case) or its long ID, in that Project.

ANTHROPIC.name: create_task
ANTHROPIC.description: Create a Project Task: supply project_id, a required title (the Task's one-line name, shown wherever the Task is listed) and a required description (the Task's content); omit status and task_id. The new Task is TODO and gets the Project's next key as its taskId (e.g. autobyteus-42). Optional context_files: absolute local file paths copied into the new Task as context files. Same file types and size limits as the app. Any invalid file fails the whole call with no change. Optional depends_on: the taskIds of Tasks of the same Project that come first (or that this Task follows up); it only informs and never stops work. Optional part_of: the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts). Returns the recorded Task (projectId, taskId, title, status, dependsOn, partOf) plus attachedContextFiles [{name, path}] when files were attached; a field with no value is left out. Does not delegate work; to give the Task to an agent, use delegate_task.

ANTHROPIC.name: update_task
ANTHROPIC.description:
Update a Task by its task_id: a Project Task (its key, e.g. autobyteus-42), or the Task a description-only delegate_task created (it has no Project; delegate_task returned its task_id). Supply title and/or description and/or status (TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, CANCELLED) and/or context_files and/or depends_on and/or part_of and/or add_comment; never project_id.
DONE means the work is finished; CANCELLED means the Task was dropped as not needed (not finished). Both end this Task's work for its task agents; a task agent is stopped when this was its last open Task; their history is kept. Close a Task you delegated when its work is done. Setting a Task that has parts to DONE or CANCELLED also sets its open parts the same way (ending their work for their task agents, as above); closedParts lists them.
To continue a closed Task with the same task agent, first set the Task to TODO or IN_PROGRESS; then, if you assigned the Task, message the task agent's run id (for a task agent team, its coordinator's run id): it continues with its conversation. A status change alone starts nothing. To give a task agent another Task, also while its other Tasks are open, use delegate_task with its target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.
Optional title (Project Tasks only): the Task's new one-line name.
Optional depends_on (Project Tasks only): the complete list of taskIds of Tasks of the same Project this Task depends on; it replaces the saved list, [] clears it. It only informs and never stops work.
Optional part_of (Project Tasks only): the taskId of the bigger Task in the same Project this Task is part of; one level only (a part can't have parts); "" clears it.
Optional add_comment (Project Tasks only): text added as a new comment at the end of the Task's comments; the description is not changed. Each call adds one comment.
Optional context_files: absolute local file paths copied into a Project Task as context files; appended, never removed. Same file types and size limits as the app; not for a Task with no Project. Any invalid file fails the whole call with no change. Unknown IDs fail; omitted fields, saved context, dependencies and the parent are kept. Returns the recorded Task identity (taskId; projectId and title for a Project Task) and status, plus dependsOn and partOf for a Project Task, attachedContextFiles [{name, path}] when the call attached files, closedParts when it closed parts and partsNotClosed when it could not close some of them; a field with no value is left out (a Task with no Project has no projectId, title, dependsOn or partOf).

ANTHROPIC.name: delegate_task
ANTHROPIC.description:
Delegate a task to an agent or agent team. Use exactly one mode:
(1) recipient_address and description, with optional reference_files: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) that works on the task you describe;
(2) recipient_address and task_id: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) for that saved Task (its description and files);
(3) exactly one of target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id, with task_id: gives the saved Task to one of your task agents (or task agent teams), which continues with its conversation; use it for follow-up work that builds on what that task agent already did. This works only when you made its most recent assignment; its other open Tasks stay open, and it is freed when its last Task is closed.
With node in mode (1), the task agent starts on that peer node, from the agent or agent team at recipient_address there; the result also gives node, and you message it by its run id as usual. A saved Task or reference_files can't go to another node.
Never supply project_id. Delegating to yourself, a teammate or your own team is refused.
The task description and reference files become the task agent's first message (for a task agent team, its coordinator receives them), together with your run id.
If you are a task agent yourself (another agent delegated your task to you or to your team), task_id is refused, and a delegation with a description returns no task_id: the new task agent's work is part of your Task. Otherwise, a delegation with a description also creates a Task with no Project and returns its task_id.
On success, delegated is true, target_kind is agent or team, and the result names the task agent: target_agent_run_id for a task agent; for a task agent team, target_team_run_id (the team; use it to give the team a later Task) and target_team_coordinator_agent_run_id (its coordinator; talk with the team through this run id). launch_notes, when present, says which agent runs on a different runtime or model than configured. If delegated is false, nothing was created and message says why; correct the problem and delegate again, or report the failure.

recipient_address.description: Only for a new task agent: the exact address of an available agent or agent team, beginning with '/'. Every call with an address creates another task agent or task agent team. Omit it when you give a Task to one of your task agents with target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.

target_team_run_id.description: One of your task agent teams, by the target_team_run_id an earlier delegation returned (the team's run id, not its coordinator's). Supply only it and task_id.

target_agent_run_id.description: One of your task agents, by the target_agent_run_id an earlier delegation returned. Supply only it and task_id. A task agent team's coordinator's run id is refused: use target_team_run_id for a task agent team.

task_id.description: A saved Project Task's ID on this node: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42), as list_project_tasks shows it; its saved text and files are used. With recipient_address: a new task agent works on the Task. With target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id: that task agent takes on the Task. Blank, unknown, ambiguous, DONE or CANCELLED Tasks fail.

description.description: Only with recipient_address and without task_id. A complete, ready-to-work task description: objective, context, scope, constraints, what done looks like, expected output and reference guidance.

ANTHROPIC.name: send_message_to
ANTHROPIC.description:
Send a self-contained request, result, question or blocker to an agent or agent team that already exists. Use exactly one selector, never both:
- recipient_address: an exact address beginning with '/'. A team's address reaches its coordinator. An address inside your own team reaches the member of your own team.
- target_agent_run_id: an agent's run id. For a task agent team, use its coordinator's run id; a team's own run id is refused.
send_message_to never creates an agent; to have work done by a new agent, use delegate_task. It returns the run id of the agent that received the message as target_agent_run_id, or leaves it out, with the reason, when the message can't be delivered.

recipient_address.description: An exact address beginning with '/'. Relative addresses, bare names and '/' alone are not valid.

target_agent_run_id.description: An agent's run id. Unknown run ids are rejected.

State the requested work or outcome and relevant context; include important absolute paths here and put files the recipient should inspect in reference_files. Example: 'Implementation is ready. The handoff is at /Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md and the test log is at /Users/me/project/test.log; please review the risks below.'

Use this in addition to self-contained content, not instead of explaining the handoff. Example: ['/Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md', '/Users/me/project/test.log'].

GEMINI.name: run_bash
GEMINI.description:
Execute a non-interactive bash command in a working directory. Any provided cwd must be an absolute path to an existing accessible local directory, including one outside the workspace. If cwd is omitted, the workspace root is used when available, otherwise the system temporary directory. cwd applies only to this invocation and does not change workspace identity or persist across calls. The result includes effectiveCwd so you can confirm where the command actually ran.

For long-running work (builds, test suites, dev servers) set run_in_background: the call returns at once with the command's pid and outputFile, and when it ends you are told its exit code (or signal) and last output lines, without polling. Read its output with `tail -n 50 <outputFile>` and stop it with `kill <pid>`, which stops everything the command started.

An `&` job of a foreground command that is still running when the foreground part ends is a background task too: the call returns, the result lists it in backgroundTasksStarted, and you are told when it ends. `kill <pid>` on such a job stops that process only; use run_in_background when you need to stop a command together with the processes it starts. Tasks started by one call share its outputFile. A background task that ends while one of your run_bash calls runs is reported in that call's backgroundTasksEnded instead of a later notice. Processes that detach themselves (nohup, setsid, disown) are not tracked. Background commands are stopped and their output files removed when your run ends.

cwd.description: Optional working directory for the command.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time in seconds for the command's foreground part. Does not apply with run_in_background.

run_in_background.description: Run the command in the background: the call returns at once with its pid and outputFile, and you are notified when it ends.

GEMINI.name: read_file
GEMINI.description: Reads content from a specified file. Supports optional 1-based inclusive line ranges via start_line/end_line. Each returned line is prefixed with its line number when include_line_numbers is true. Image, audio and video files (by extension) are attached for the model to see in the next turn instead of being returned as text; line ranges do not apply to them, a kind the current model cannot take is refused, and other binary files are refused. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute base_dir and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell cd state. Raises ValueError if a relative path is given without an absolute base_dir or if line range arguments are invalid. Raises FileNotFoundError if the file does not exist. Raises IOError if file reading fails for other reasons.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path, or a relative file path paired with base_dir. If path is relative, you must provide an absolute base_dir. If base_dir is omitted, path must be absolute. Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. Do not provide a relative base_dir.

start_line.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Text files only; omit to start at line 1.

end_line.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Text files only; omit to read to the end.

include_line_numbers.description: If true, prefix each returned line with its line number (default).

GEMINI.name: edit_file
GEMINI.description: Applies a context-located patch to one file using a simplified unified-diff-style format, without overwriting unrelated content. Before calling `edit_file`, read the current relevant file region unless it was just read and has not changed. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from that latest content; do not reconstruct them from memory. After an intervening edit or a context-match failure, read the affected region again before retrying. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute `base_dir` and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell `cd` state. Use this for surgical edits; use `write_file` only for a deliberate whole-file rewrite.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path, or a relative file path paired with base_dir. If path is relative, you must provide an absolute base_dir. If base_dir is omitted, path must be absolute. Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. Do not provide a relative base_dir.

patch.description:
Patch content in a simplified unified-diff-style format. Start every hunk with a bare `@@` line. Prefix unchanged lines with one space, removals with `-`, and additions with `+`. Every prefixed hunk body record is a complete logical line even if the outer patch string has no final line ending. Outer patch-string termination is transport framing, not target-file semantics. To make changed target content end without a line terminator, immediately follow that record with the exact marker `\ No newline at end of file`; this marker is the sole opt-out from a changed record's normal line terminator. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from the latest current file content. The target file is identified by the separate `path` argument; inside `patch`, provide only bare context hunks. Do not include Git file headers (`diff --git`, `---`, or `+++`), numeric hunk coordinates, or semantic envelopes such as `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch`. Include enough unchanged or removal lines to identify exactly one eligible location.

Example patch:
@@
-const mode = 'old'
+const mode = 'new'
 const keep = true

'content' is the string content to write. Creates parent directories if they don't exist. Raises ValueError if a relative path is given without an absolute base_dir. Raises IOError if file writing fails.

function.name: run_bash
function.description:
Execute a non-interactive bash command in a working directory. Any provided cwd must be an absolute path to an existing accessible local directory, including one outside the workspace. If cwd is omitted, the workspace root is used when available, otherwise the system temporary directory. cwd applies only to this invocation and does not change workspace identity or persist across calls. The result includes effectiveCwd so you can confirm where the command actually ran.

For long-running work (builds, test suites, dev servers) set run_in_background: the call returns at once with the command's pid and outputFile, and when it ends you are told its exit code (or signal) and last output lines, without polling. Read its output with `tail -n 50 <outputFile>` and stop it with `kill <pid>`, which stops everything the command started.

An `&` job of a foreground command that is still running when the foreground part ends is a background task too: the call returns, the result lists it in backgroundTasksStarted, and you are told when it ends. `kill <pid>` on such a job stops that process only; use run_in_background when you need to stop a command together with the processes it starts. Tasks started by one call share its outputFile. A background task that ends while one of your run_bash calls runs is reported in that call's backgroundTasksEnded instead of a later notice. Processes that detach themselves (nohup, setsid, disown) are not tracked. Background commands are stopped and their output files removed when your run ends.

cwd.description: Optional working directory for the command.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time in seconds for the command's foreground part. Does not apply with run_in_background.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Applies a context-located patch to one file using a simplified unified-diff-style format, without overwriting unrelated content. Before calling `edit_file`, read the current relevant file region unless it was just read and has not changed. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from that latest content; do not reconstruct them from memory. After an intervening edit or a context-match failure, read the affected region again before retrying. File paths use trusted-local semantics: absolute paths are used directly; relative paths require an explicit absolute `base_dir` and are never resolved from workspace, process, or shell `cd` state. Use this for surgical edits; use `write_file` only for a deliberate whole-file rewrite.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path, or a relative file path paired with base_dir. If path is relative, you must provide an absolute base_dir. If base_dir is omitted, path must be absolute. Absolute paths are used directly and take precedence if base_dir is also supplied. Relative paths are never resolved from the configured workspace, process cwd, or prior shell cd state.

base_dir.description: Optional absolute directory used only when path is relative; it is required for a relative path. If path is absolute, omit base_dir (an absolute path takes precedence if both are supplied). This applies to this tool call only and does not change shell or agent working-directory state. Do not provide a relative base_dir.

patch.description:
Patch content in a simplified unified-diff-style format. Start every hunk with a bare `@@` line. Prefix unchanged lines with one space, removals with `-`, and additions with `+`. Every prefixed hunk body record is a complete logical line even if the outer patch string has no final line ending. Outer patch-string termination is transport framing, not target-file semantics. To make changed target content end without a line terminator, immediately follow that record with the exact marker `\ No newline at end of file`; this marker is the sole opt-out from a changed record's normal line terminator. Copy unchanged and removal lines exactly from the latest current file content. The target file is identified by the separate `path` argument; inside `patch`, provide only bare context hunks. Do not include Git file headers (`diff --git`, `---`, or `+++`), numeric hunk coordinates, or semantic envelopes such as `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch`. Include enough unchanged or removal lines to identify exactly one eligible location.

Example patch:
@@
-const mode = 'old'
+const mode = 'new'
 const keep = true

(3) exactly one of target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id, with task_id: gives the saved Task to one of your task agents (or task agent teams), which continues with its conversation; use it for follow-up work that builds on what that task agent already did. This works only when you made its most recent assignment; its other open Tasks stay open, and it is freed when its last Task is closed.
With node in mode (1), the task agent starts on that peer node, from the agent or agent team at recipient_address there; the result also gives node, and you message it by its run id as usual. A saved Task or reference_files can't go to another node.
Never supply project_id. Delegating to yourself, a teammate or your own team is refused.
The task description and reference files become the task agent's first message (for a task agent team, its coordinator receives them), together with your run id.
If you are a task agent yourself (another agent delegated your task to you or to your team), task_id is refused, and a delegation with a description returns no task_id: the new task agent's work is part of your Task. GEMINI.name: list_available_agents
GEMINI.description: List the agents and agent teams you can work with, each with its name, kind (agent or agent_team), address and description (when it has one). GEMINI.name: send_message_to
GEMINI.description:
Send a self-contained request, result, question or blocker to an agent or agent team that already exists. Use exactly one selector, never both:
- recipient_address: an exact address beginning with '/'. A team's address reaches its coordinator. An address inside your own team reaches the member of your own team.
- target_agent_run_id: an agent's run id. For a task agent team, use its coordinator's run id; a team's own run id is refused.
send_message_to never creates an agent; to have work done by a new agent, use delegate_task. It returns the run id of the agent that received the message as target_agent_run_id, or leaves it out, with the reason, when the message can't be delivered.

recipient_address.description: An exact address beginning with '/'. Relative addresses, bare names and '/' alone are not valid.

target_agent_run_id.description: An agent's run id. Unknown run ids are rejected.

content.description: Self-contained work request, result, or specific blocker. State the requested work or outcome and relevant context; include important absolute paths here and put files the recipient should inspect in reference_files. Example: 'Implementation is ready. The handoff is at /Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md and the test log is at /Users/me/project/test.log; please review the risks below.'

reference_files.description: Optional attachment/reference list of absolute local file paths the recipient may need to inspect. Use this in addition to self-contained content, not instead of explaining the handoff. Example: ['/Users/me/project/implementation-handoff.md', '/Users/me/project/test.log'].

GEMINI.name: delegate_task
GEMINI.description:
Delegate a task to an agent or agent team. Use exactly one mode:
(1) recipient_address and description, with optional reference_files: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) that works on the task you describe;
(2) recipient_address and task_id: creates a new task agent (or task agent team) for that saved Task (its description and files);
(3) exactly one of target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id, with task_id: gives the saved Task to one of your task agents (or task agent teams), which continues with its conversation; use it for follow-up work that builds on what that task agent already did. This works only when you made its most recent assignment; its other open Tasks stay open, and it is freed when its last Task is closed.
With node in mode (1), the task agent starts on that peer node, from the agent or agent team at recipient_address there; the result also gives node, and you message it by its run id as usual. A saved Task or reference_files can't go to another node.
Never supply project_id. Delegating to yourself, a teammate or your own team is refused.
The task description and reference files become the task agent's first message (for a task agent team, its coordinator receives them), together with your run id.
If you are a task agent yourself (another agent delegated your task to you or to your team), task_id is refused, and a delegation with a description returns no task_id: the new task agent's work is part of your Task. Otherwise, a delegation with a description also creates a Task with no Project and returns its task_id.
On success, delegated is true, target_kind is agent or team, and the result names the task agent: target_agent_run_id for a task agent; for a task agent team, target_team_run_id (the team; use it to give the team a later Task) and target_team_coordinator_agent_run_id (its coordinator; talk with the team through this run id). launch_notes, when present, says which agent runs on a different runtime or model than configured. If delegated is false, nothing was created and message says why; correct the problem and delegate again, or report the failure.

recipient_address.description: Only for a new task agent: the exact address of an available agent or agent team, beginning with '/'. Every call with an address creates another task agent or task agent team. Omit it when you give a Task to one of your task agents with target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id.

target_team_run_id.description: One of your task agent teams, by the target_team_run_id an earlier delegation returned (the team's run id, not its coordinator's). Supply only it and task_id.

target_agent_run_id.description: One of your task agents, by the target_agent_run_id an earlier delegation returned. Supply only it and task_id. A task agent team's coordinator's run id is refused: use target_team_run_id for a task agent team.

task_id.description: A saved Project Task's ID on this node: its key (e.g. autobyteus-42), as list_project_tasks shows it; its saved text and files are used. With recipient_address: a new task agent works on the Task. With target_agent_run_id or target_team_run_id: that task agent takes on the Task. Blank, unknown, ambiguous, DONE or CANCELLED Tasks fail.

description.description: Only with recipient_address and without task_id. A complete, ready-to-work task description: objective, context, scope, constraints, what done looks like, expected output and reference guidance.

node.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description: the name of a peer node registered on this node. The new task agent then runs on that node, and recipient_address is the address of an agent or agent team on that node.

reference_files.description: Optional, only with recipient_address and description; not allowed with task_id, not even as an empty list. Absolute local file paths the task agent should read. Relative paths and URLs are rejected.

GEMINI.name: search_memory
GEMINI.description: Search the memory of all agent runs on this node (their Work Journals: what each run did, with dates) by words and by meaning, in any language. Use it whenever the user or the task refers to earlier work: "do you remember", "last time", "earlier we", "before", "where is the … we set up", or a decision, setup or file made in a past conversation. Returns up to limit runs (1 to 20; default from the server setting, normally 10), best first. Each result names who (agent, and team or org with member when there is one), runId, workspace, the first and latest day mentioned, a source line to cite, and its matches: journalFile (an absolute path), lines, day, a short snippet and matchedBy. A text match lists the query words it contains (matchedWords); a match without matchedWords was found by meaning. wordsNotFound names query words that occur in no indexed journal (the index follows new turns within about a minute). Results are pointers, not facts: open a run's first match (its newest) at its lines with your file tool before answering, and the second when the first does not answer, before searching again. Answer from the run you read and cite its source. When several runs differ, prefer the latest mention and say so. If what you read does not answer the question, try other words. coverage says how much is indexed while indexing is incomplete; with no index yet, ask the user to start it on the Memory page.

query.description: What you are looking for, in your own words, any language: a sentence or a few words.

limit.description: Most runs returned, 1 to 20 (default from the server setting).
